title: THE LORD-INQUISITOR'S OFFICE
revisit: Her office. A dossier on the desk, and a woman who has been useful to you for a fortnight.
intro:
She has been useful for a fortnight.

A transport writ fixed in an afternoon when the Munitorum said nine days. An
informant flagged as unreliable before you wasted a week on him. A note asking
after Bez's cough, in her own hand, which she did not have to send.

And on the eleventh night, at the third hour, an Arbites hold on tier two that
you were pulled out of by a Lord-Inquisitor who had been woken up and did not
mention it afterwards.

There is a dossier on the desk when you come in. She does not push it across.

"Sit down," Crase says. "I want to ask you for something and I want to do it
properly, which means you get to say no."
look:
An office with two chairs and no ornaments in it.

The DOSSIER on the desk, not pushed across.
Inquisitor CRASE, who has been useful for a fortnight.

objects.careless: A dossier on the Ferrum Gallery. Thick. Somebody has worked on this for months and it was not started this week.
objects.careful:
It is good work. That is the first thing and it does not stop being the thing.

Fourth-generation genestealer infestation in Shift Nine of the Ferrum Gallery. Into three shift-councils and the coolant guild. Birth-defect returns bent four ways across nineteen years; medicae records that stop being medicae records in 'ninety-two; a shift foreman whose personnel file has been amended eleven times by four different offices.

The evidence is real, it is thorough, and it is correct. There is a cult in the Ferrum Gallery and it has been there for four generations and somebody is going to have to go down there.

None of that is in question. What is in question is why this dossier is on this desk in this fortnight.

npcs.title: Inquisitor Yolanda Crase
npcs.topic_refusal: "Ask," Crase says. "I've asked you for something; you're owed a few."
npcs.portrait: Inquisitor Yolanda Crase. Six years Lord-Inquisitor, a fortnight of small kindnesses, and a dossier she has not pushed across the desk.
npcs.greeting:
"I'm not going to dress this up and I'm not going to order you," Crase says. "I could. I'm not going to.

"There is a genestealer cult in the Ferrum Gallery. Fourth generation, into three shift-councils and the coolant guild, and it has been there since before either of us held a rosette. It is real, the evidence is in that folder, and it is the largest single thing on this world that anybody can actually do something about.

"It will take you three weeks and it will probably work."

She folds her hands.

"Hadrian's business is eleven weeks old and cold and it has got you nowhere in a fortnight. I am asking you to put it down and go and do this one."
npcs.reprise: She waits. She is not going to ask twice and she is not going to sulk.
npcs.unknown: "I don't know," Crase says. "I'd find out, if it mattered."
deflect: "Not today," she says, and means it kindly.

topics.text:
"Because it's ready and you're the officer with the time."

It is a completely adequate answer. It is the answer she would have given at any point in the last six years about anything, and it is true.

"And Hadrian?"

"Hadrian is dead, and I have read your file notes, and there is nothing in them." She says it gently and it lands like a slap because it is accurate. "You have a savant who contradicts himself, a purge order from before you were born, and a Cardinal who has been selling confession for forty years — which is real, and which you should file, and which has nothing whatever to do with a man shooting himself in a sealed room.

"I am not managing you. I am telling you what your fortnight looks like from this desk."

"It is real," Crase says, "and I want you to satisfy yourself of that rather than take it from me."

So you do. It takes ninety minutes and she does not interrupt once.

The returns are bent. The medicae records stop. The foreman's file has been amended eleven times by four offices and two of the offices no longer exist. There is a fourth-generation infestation in Shift Nine of the Ferrum Gallery and it has been there for eighty years and it is going to have to be dealt with by somebody.

Everything in the folder is true.

That is not the same as it being the reason it is on the desk, and you are going to spend a long time not being able to separate those two things.

You put the lift log in front of her.

Crase reads it, and does not pretend to be surprised, and does not stop doing it either.

"Yes," she says. "Since the fourteenth. Two of my people, in rotation, and a third on the Spire when you go up."

"You didn't tell me."

"No." She sets the log down. "You are an Inquisitor of one fortnight's standing who has been in an Arbites hold at the third hour, in a condemned outflow pipe in a district that does not exist, and in a Cardinal's private confessional alone. I have lost one Inquisitor this month.

"I am not sorry and I am not going to stop."

She looks at you with an expression you have seen once before, in a doorway, at the fourth hour.

"You'd do the same," she says. "You will do the same."

"I had a note from the medicae deck," Crase says. "Not about you — about the Sergeant. Ostro is not supposed to send those and sends them anyway, which is why I like him.

"Fourteen months."

She does not make a speech about it.

"She won't take a discharge and I won't offer her one, because offering it is the same as saying it out loud in front of her, and she has arranged twenty-six years around not having that conversation.

"Use her. She'd rather be used than looked after. But do not let her carry anything up a stair for you and then tell yourself she volunteered."

acts.text:
You take it.

Fourteen days. It is real work and it is good work and you are good at it, and there is a genuine fourth-generation infestation in Shift Nine and by the end of it there is not.

Crase is delighted with you in a way she has not been since the antechamber, and says so, and means it.

When you come back up, Hadrian Vosk has been dead for five weeks and the flush order for the Rows is dated day forty and day forty was eleven days ago.

[ DECOY_PURSUED — CRASE_STANDING +3 ]

You say no.

Crase nods once, takes the dossier back, and says "right" in a completely ordinary voice, and then asks whether you have eaten.

That is the entire conversation. There is no speech and no reproach and nothing further is said about it, that day or any other.

What happens instead, over the following week:

Your requisitions come back about forty per cent slower. Two of Vosk's old contacts stop answering. A note arrives asking after the Sergeant's cough, in Crase's own hand, warm and unforced.

And the Crown lift log records your rosette at sub-level nine at 04:12.

You were asleep at 04:12, in a chair, in a room with the door bolted, and you know that because you woke with the bolt still across.

There is no sub-level nine in the Adamant Crown. There are eight. You have counted them. You count them again on the way down and there are eight.

[ DECOY_REFUSED ]

exits.text: Out, and down one tier, to a room with no shadow in it.

B13a.label: Crase's Ferrum Gallery dossier — a real fourth-generation infestation, thoroughly evidenced, offered this fortnight
B13a.file_text:
FILED. CLASS: XENOS / CULT — ACTIVE. INDEXED. REQUISITION-ELIGIBLE.

The cogitator indexes it in four seconds and offers to open it as your principal matter, which would supersede the Vosk file, which is dormant.

It phrases this as a convenience.
B13a.note_text:
You write down what is in it and, underneath, the date it was compiled, and underneath that the date it was put on the desk.

The first two are eleven months apart. The second and third are a fortnight.

Everything in the folder is true. That is not the same as being the reason it is on the desk, and you are not going to be able to separate those two things for a long time.

strings.already_read: You have read it twice. She is waiting.
strings.no_terminal: Her terminal, not yours. She would let you. That is not the point.
